newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish deputy resigns in boost to Yilmaz.
newsitem.headline: Turkish deputy resigns in boost to Yilmaz.

text.p: A Turkish MP resigned from an opposition party on Friday, boosting Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz a day ahead of a confidence vote in the new anti-Islamist government.
Demir Berberoglu, head of parliament's human rights committee, quit the conservative True Path Party (DYP) with a three-page letter sent to the parliamentary speaker's office.
"I am leaving the DYP until unity on the right is achieved and politics come into line with the real situation in the country," the letter said.
Yilmaz, head of a rival right-wing party, has more than a dozen more deputies on paper than he needs to win Saturday's vote in the 550-seat assembly.
He has been aided by a wave of recent defections from the True Path. It was not immediately clear whether Berberoglu would support the government in the vote.
A key leftist party with 49 deputies pledged support for the left-right coalition at a debate on the government programme on Thursday.
Islamist former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned last month after a long, bitter row with the secularist military over religious activism.
The new government has said it will hold early elections next year, well before polls are due in the year 2000.
Berberoglu called on his True Path former colleagues to overthrow party leader Tansu Ciller and announce a pardon for recent defectors.
"I hope that the colleagues I have left behind will be able to achieve the resignation of the chairman and declare a political pardon," he said.
Ciller, who became Turkey's first woman leader in 1993, has been criticised by the secularists for joining the Islamists in coalition last year.
